title: Catalogue curation and cross-domain promotion

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Approved rationale, scope, preservation boundaries, exemplar promotion criteria, and stop conditions.

allowedWork: Catalogue in-shell selection, history restoration, focus and review preservation, surface-aware stage geometry, compact visual step layout, and bounded editorial curation.
One exact supply-and-demand equilibrium asset and one exact constant-force work-energy asset using existing runtime, host, graph, equation, diagram, accessibility, and review seams.
Post-checkpoint API classification, caller-proven synchronized-model seams, versioned motif boundaries, and adjacent complexity-negative pruning.
Focused tests, stable browser checks, release verification, and project-memory reconciliation directly required by this tranche.
disallowedWork: Visual generalization before the corresponding human exemplar checkpoint is approved.
A universal renderer, scene graph, parameter schema, motif registry, economics solver, physics engine, or parallel runtime and clock.
Programming trace implementation, public website, curriculum, learner systems, broad LLM editorial work, or unrelated dashboard work.
Broad route deletion, inferred human dispositions, deletion of semantic fixtures, or pruning without last-caller evidence.
goal: Make catalogue review seamless, promote bounded economics and physics exemplars, then consolidate only seams proven by both callers.
commitCadence: Commit each independently reversible verified slice with its Theseus evidence; stop at s08, s22, and s27 for human exemplar review before continuing.
stopConditions: Stop at s08 until the user explicitly approves the live catalogue UX exemplar.
Stop at s22 until the user explicitly approves the live economics exemplar.
Stop at s27 until the user explicitly approves the live physics second caller.
Stop if presentation simplification requires semantic, runtime, clock, renderer, paint-ownership, accessibility, review-history, or authoring-contract changes.
Stop if a bounded domain exemplar requires an economics solver, physics engine, universal renderer, scene graph, or parallel runtime.
Stop before shared API or motif extraction unless two approved structurally different callers prove the same invariant.
Stop before pruning when any unique semantic, conformance, compatibility, or historical evidence remains.
Stop when verification evidence is missing, contradictory, or cannot be recorded durably.

slices.title: Align durable project direction
slices.summary: Aligned durable direction around the approved successor order. Roadmap, current queue, catalogue, promotion, and cross-domain threads now name persistent catalogue UX and curation, then rank-3 economics, rank-4 physics, and caller-proven consolidation. Superseded the stale BFS-gated economics action and recorded the user-requested priority change. Promotion memory, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.

slices.title: Freeze catalogue interaction baseline
slices.summary: Extended the stable catalogue visual command with a browser-observed full-navigation before-state from solve-x to radical. It proves document, shell, and review composer replacement plus reset query, Details mode, and empty draft, while preserving correct asset URL and 33-row hostability. Published the desired selected-asset-only replacement boundary. Typecheck, visual catalogue, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.

slices.title: Define persistent selection controller
slices.summary: Added a pure typed catalogue navigation controller. Ordinary same-origin same-path known-asset links produce pushed in-shell selections; same-row links stay; prevented, non-primary, modified, targeted, download, cross-origin, cross-path, other-view, and unknown links retain native fallback. History distinguishes known selection with bounded playhead, unknown artifact, and leaving the catalogue. Six focused tests, typecheck, architecture, and diff hygiene pass; main browser lifecycle is unchanged.

slices.title: Implement in-shell asset switching
slices.summary: Implemented bounded in-shell asset switching. Known ordinary catalogue links push a clean asset URL and replace only stage, inspector, and player ownership; shell, rail query, inspector mode, review composer, and unsaved draft persist. Native fallbacks remain intact. Stable browser proof covers the interaction plus all 33 host rows; 3202 tests, production build and typecheck, review-production boundary, impact selection, and diff hygiene pass. Back and forward plus explicit focus proof remain s05.

slices.title: Prove history focus and review preservation
slices.summary: Added catalogue-aware popstate restoration while keeping non-catalogue routing bounded to the existing view dispatcher. In-shell selection now snapshots and restores replaced row, player, inspector-view, and tuning focus without stealing newly moved focus, and preserves the rail viewport. Stable browser evidence proves Back and Forward asset restoration plus document, shell, query, inspector, rail, review host, draft, selected-row focus, inspector focus, search focus, and review-composer focus preservation. Typecheck, 3202 tests, production build, review boundary, 33-host capture, and diff hygiene pass.

slices.title: Build solve-x centered compact-stage exemplar
slices.summary: Built the solve-x-only catalogue visual exemplar. A selection-scoped CSS boundary groups the previously independent transition and step nodes into one centered 48rem-or-narrower unit, centers the inline equation, and constrains all four step chips to compact intrinsic height. Playback controls stay fixed below and the runtime, timeline, semantic model, renderer, paint ownership, accessibility, and authoring contracts are unchanged. Stable visual interaction and 33-host smoke plus diff hygiene pass.

slices.title: Capture catalogue UX exemplar
slices.summary: Published deterministic catalogue UX checkpoint evidence. The stable browser command now measures solve-x centering, compact content and step height, and no-document-scroll control visibility; captures both start and 50 percent frames; retains the in-shell history, focus, review, and 33-host proofs; and emits all evidence in its manifest. Added a concise review note naming the live URL, acceptance evidence, preservation boundary, promotion meaning, and exact rollback units. Visual capture, typecheck, and diff hygiene pass.

slices.title: Human review catalogue UX
slices.summary: HUMAN APPROVED. The user explicitly approved the live persistent catalogue interaction and solve-x centered compact-stage direction. This authorizes s09 to generalize only surface-compatible geometry proven against structurally different callers; it does not authorize universal dimensions, runtime changes, or semantic/renderer/authoring changes.

slices.title: Generalize approved stage geometry
slices.summary: Generalized the human-approved, surface-compatible centering seam across catalogue equation stages only. Equation content now forms one full-width centered grid with centered native math; exact width and compact step styling remain solve-x-specific. The structurally different radical caller proves compact centering without inheriting solve-x dimensions, while the exact-fraction diagram caller proves the CSS boundary does not leak across render targets. Stable pressure manifests, interaction/history/focus/review checks, reduced-motion and narrow checks, all 33 hosts, typecheck, and diff hygiene pass.

slices.title: Record bounded catalogue curation
slices.summary: Recorded bounded curation without new UI or inferred dispositions. All 33 concrete rows remain; solve-x, radical, and exact-fraction roles are explicit; Jacobian/Hessian is a gated diagnostic/retirement candidate; provisional incorrect substitution remains disclosed negative evidence; programming stays deferred; roadmap and active thread now advance to economics. Promotion memory, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.

slices.title: Freeze economics model contract
slices.summary: Froze the exemplar-first economics contract: Q horizontal, P vertical, supply P=2+Q, demand P=14-Q shifting to P=18-Q, exact equilibrium (6,8) to (8,10), stable curve/parameter/side/claim roles, no solver or new runtime category. Published acceptance, preservation, and rollback boundaries. Two focused tests, all TypeScript projects, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.

slices.title: Implement exact supply-demand model
slices.summary: Implemented the bounded exact rational supply-demand model. It validates axes, positive slopes, and upward demand-intercept shift; solves exact before/after intersections; evaluates both curves; classifies surplus, shortage, and clearing with exact magnitudes; normalizes and freezes serializable state. Default and fractional cases plus invalid inputs pass six focused tests; typecheck, architecture, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.

slices.title: Project deterministic economics frames
slices.summary: Added renderer-neutral exact economics frames. Each frame preserves Q/P axes, supply, demand, equilibrium, intercept-parameter, surplus-side, shortage-side, and active semantic identities while interpolating exact rational model truth; midpoint is demand P=16-Q and equilibrium (7,9). Forward t and rewind 1-t produce identical model states. Ten economics tests, typecheck, architecture, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.

slices.title: Define economics graph surface semantics
slices.summary: Defined isolated economics graph-surface semantics as a native KpAnimationAsset without registering or rendering it. Persistent graph, Q/P axes, supply, demand, intercept parameter, equilibrium role, surplus/shortage sides, exact source/target states, and one shiftDemandIntercept transformation close references and preserve required correspondences. Thirteen economics tests, typecheck, architecture, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.

slices.title: Render static equilibrium view
slices.summary: Rendered the exact initial economics state through the existing native SVG graph viewport. The shared viewport still owns grid and axes; an isolated presenter paints supply, initial demand, exact (6,8) equilibrium, guides, Q/P labels, and deterministic data evidence with one canonical owner. No catalogue registration or motion yet. Fifteen economics tests, typecheck, architecture, diff hygiene, and workspace validation pass.
